To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the use of management accounting practices in support lean strategy in service organizations is limited and that there are some differences in this regard between the Accounting Department and operational departments.

1) there is a positive association between lean practices in operational departments and the use of specific management accounting systems; 2) there is a lack of a positive association between the use of management accounting practices and the support of top management for lean initiatives; and 3) there is a need for a more detailed financial information in the operational departments, which is currently not provided by the Accounting Department.
there are positive and significant associations between lean practices and whiteboard use and employee empowerment.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of how the management accounting system can be used to support a lean management strategy in a service organization.
the following research question: To what extent are specific management accounting practices (MAS) used by service companies to support lean initiatives?
the question of whether management accounting supports lean strategy.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
management accounting practices in the studied company are not yet sufficiently developed in support of lean practices.
there is a significant association between lean strategy and MAS practices.
the management accounting system, in the case of the company analyzed, does not yet fully support lean management practices.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
management accounting practices in support lean management strategy are still in a process of development and that the Accounting Department has a lot to do to make them more effective.
the management accounting system is still, in a part, a set a data and not a way of action, what is contrary to lean management philosophy.
management accounting practices in support for lean management strategy are still in their infancy.
The main takeaway from our work is that
management accounting systems are changing in response to lean strategy.
the management accounting system is still, in some respects, a set of information and not a mode action.
lean strategy can be supported by management accounting tools and practices, but it is not clear whether these are sufficient to support a lean management system.
